Subject: Downstream vendor accreditation — Order Form amendment request

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the call earlier. As discussed, VectorScale is adding a managed log-transport vendor into the delivery chain for the analytics ingestion tied to our POC. Our procurement team needs a short Order Form amendment confirming: (1) whether Redwood will accept the downstream vendor as a subprocessor for log delivery; (2) the limited DPA scoping for logs that include customer identifiers; and (3) what evidence Redwood can provide for custody and encryption at rest in transit for that vendor.

I've attached our proposed redlines to the Order Form and a zip with the vendor's SOC-like attestation. We're targeting sign-off by Oct 6 to avoid a delivery delay. Can you please route to your legal and procurement? We can be flexible on language but need a concise path (amendment + DPA addendum or short Annex).

Attachments: VectorScale_redlines_20260930.docx; downstream_evidence_bundle_0926.zip

Best,
Sara
Sara Patel

Kimberly / Jonas,

Forwarding VectorScale's request (below). Key asks: accept downstream vendor as subprocessor on Order Form; narrow DPA scoping for logs containing PII; and produce custody/encryption evidence. They prefer an Order Form amendment + DPA annex (short).

Quick notes from product: the vendor will only receive encrypted log bundles via S3 with KMS-managed keys; no inference workloads run externally. Ops says we can provide transfer logs and KMS key IDs; they do not have a SOC2 report, only a self-attestation (in the zip).

Requesting legal input on two items:
- Whether we can accept the downstream vendor under a limited flowdown (Order Form clause + DPA Annex) without a full subprocessor approval process that requires a DocuSign MSA amendment.
- The minimal evidence package we can require (we should avoid indefinite procurement delay).

Can we aim for a short Annex template + a statement of evidence (S3 transfer logs + KMS thumbprint) and delegate signature authority to me (contracts) for this Order Form amendment?

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Downstream vendor accreditation — Order Form amendment request

On Wed, Sep 30, 2026 at 11:02 AM Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding VectorScale's request (below). Key asks: accept downstream vendor as subprocessor on Order Form; narrow DPA scoping for logs containing PII; and produce custody/encryption evidence.

Thanks for the context — clear and helpful.

We can avoid a full MSA amendment if the change is limited in scope and the Order Form includes: (a) explicit naming of the downstream vendor and permitted processing; (b) a DPA Annex referencing the upstream DPA and specifying that Redwood remains controller/processor boundaries and liability is unchanged; and (c) a required evidence checklist (transfer logs, KMS key fingerprint, and an attestation signed by an officer of the downstream vendor).

Two legal caveats: (1) any broad delegation of signature authority beyond contract team requires Exec (GC) sign-off; limited delegation to you for Order Form amendments is fine if we keep the Annex to a single page and require a post-execution evidence deliverable. (2) If VectorScale requires the downstream vendor to have third-party audits (SOC2), we should push for an alternative: periodic attestation + right-to-audit clause with 30 days' notice.

Ask: Marcus, draft a one-page Annex (template language below) and include the evidence checklist. Attach that to the Order Form and route to VectorScale. I'll review and, if language is within the guardrails, you may sign.

Proposed short Annex bullets:
- Named Subprocessor: [Vendor Name]
- Purpose: secure transfer and transient storage of log bundles for ingestion
- Data scope: logs identified in Order Form, limited to the fields listed in Appendix A (PII marker only)
- Security controls: AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit, KMS key IDs to be provided
- Evidence required within 10 business days post-execution: S3 transfer logs, signed attestation PDF, KMS key thumbprint
- Right to audit: Redwood may request audit with 30 days' notice; scope limited to processing activities related to VectorScale delivery

I will attach example language. Jonas — FYI for procurement escalation; please flag any commercial blockers.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@vectorscale.com>

Marcus / Kimberly,

Thanks — that approach works for us. We've attached one more attestation from the vendor (signed) and a short commercial note: VectorScale prefers that Redwood accept the Annex and evidence package instead of requiring a SOC2, since the vendor is a small specialist partner. We can accept the right-to-audit and the 10-business-day evidence window.

Next steps:
- Marcus to send a one-page Annex + updated Order Form redline (we've included a cleaned list of log fields in Appendix A).
- VectorScale to confirm the final vendor name (will confirm by Monday) and upload the signed attestation.
- Once Annex is agreed, Marcus will request DocuSign for Order Form amendment; VectorScale will countersign.

I'll upload the attestation now.

Attachments: vendor_attestation_signed_1002.pdf

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sara
